emma.s: Heads-up — Pricing Grid v3 goes live later today. Quick question: for inbound POCs where the customer requests a short-term promotional discount (not a commit), what’s the internal path for approval?

omar.d: Short answer: we have a POC-exception flow. Longer: submit the POC Exception Request form, attach the commercial justification + expected ARR pipeline, and route to Deal Desk for approval. If >30% discount or >$50k ARR impact, escalate to RevOps.

jia.w: Adding detail: the form is here: https://redwood.internal/sales/poc-exception-form and the rate-limit matrix is in the Pricing Grid doc (see v3 section). For non-commit promos we require: customer name, ACV estimate, duration of promo, SKU mapping, and fallback billing plan after POC.

max.k: For technical presales: can we just apply a promo code on the billing side while running the POC, or does it need a special SKU?

omar.d: Prefer SKUs mapped to the promo. Promo codes are supported for self-serve but for enterprise POCs we create a one-off SKU/line item in the quote so finance has a clear audit trail.

emma.s: Is there a standard max duration for POC promos? Customer asked for 6 months.

jia.w: Default max is 90 days (3 months). Anything >90 days requires Deal Desk + RevOps signoff and a Product/Legal check for any special usage caps.

omar.d: Approvals checklist (copy for quick reference):
1) POC Exception form filled
2) Commercial justification (pipeline + conversion hypothesis)
3) SKU mapping and fallback plan
4) Deal Desk sign-off (omar.d)
5) RevOps if >30% discount or >$50k
6) Legal review for >90 days or data residency exceptions

max.k: Helpful — would be great to have a tiny justification template for AE/Solutions to paste.

jia.w: Sure — use this snippet in the form:```
Conversion hypothesis: customer expects X% conversion to paid within Y months; expected ACV = $Z. Promo required to remove vendor lock and validate integration. Promo duration requested: N days. Fallback product/price: <SKU-XXXXX>.
Key risks: low usage during POC, success criteria: <list>.```

omar.d: Also note: for any promo that touches Dedicated or Private plans (reserved capacity) we treat it as a commit-equivalent and require at least a 6-month minimum or equivalent financial guarantee.

emma.s: And grandfathering for existing customers who ask to keep an old rate?

omar.d: We avoid ad-hoc grandfathering. Exceptions only by Deal Desk + Head of Revenue for strategic accounts. Document requested changes in the rate change matrix and include migration assistance plan.

dealbot: Pricing Grid v3 published — https://redwood.internal/docs/pricing-grid-v3 — effective 2026-04-01. See changelog for promo and POC exception rules. :package:

emma.s: Great, we'll link the form in the AE playbook and call out the 90-day default. @omar.d @jia.w will ping you if we hit a >90d ask. :thumbsup:

omar.d: Thanks — please CC deal-desk@redwood.com on the form so we get automated routing.

jia.w: I'll update the sales playbook and add the justification snippet in the AE template. :memo:

max.k: Nice — one more ask: can we get a short decision SLA for Deal Desk on these POCs? 48 hours would be ideal.

omar.d: We'll aim for 48 hours for standard POC exceptions during business days; flag anything urgent in the subject and we'll expedite.

emma.s: Awesome — closing this thread and will post the playbook update.
